start.scope: task_name_for_pid and TASK_POWER_INFO_V2 for app PID 91886 only

additional_task_power_counters.scope: TASK_POWER_INFO_V2 counters for the app process. GPU time excludes WindowServer. Task CPU-energy accounting is not whole-device energy or battery consumption; helpers are excluded.

child_cpu_observation.scope: Kernel accounting for completed child processes over this additional observation interval; this interval starts later than the main measurement and includes sleep. No full-system CPU or battery inference is made.

limits: Finite tests and a one-hour run cannot prove zero bugs or universally minimal resource usage.
The run observes this installed app in the background with recorded Settings open/close checks while the Mac is available for normal use; it is not a controlled benchmark of all UI interactions.
CPU, memory, wakeups and disk counters cover the app process only. OS helpers, networking services, cfprefsd and WindowServer are excluded.
No full battery discharge or attributable power measurement was performed. AC power readings are recorded; battery duration is not inferred from CPU usage.
System sleep and DarkWake occurred during the measurement and were observed in pmset logs. This was not a deliberately controlled sleep/wake experiment. No multi-day endurance run was performed.
Paid-account quotas were not deliberately exhausted. Alert transitions use labeled samples and deterministic fixtures; background usage fetches use actual providers.
Runtime testing covers this Apple Silicon macOS system. Intel and older macOS runtime behavior remain untested.

The macOS window-sharing indicator emitted geometry diagnostics during capture. The symbolicated stack points to NSThemeFrame._positionSharingIndicator and NSWindowSharingSessionRecipientIndicator; a separate Settings-window probe emitted no matching runtime issue. These OS-path diagnostics were recorded, not eliminated.

A temporary Mac lock prevented one in-run Settings inspection. After the run, Settings was accessible and both sample notifications were delivered again. The live menu popup was not directly clicked by automation; menu rendering and event-tracking behavior were covered by separate AppKit tests.
